M. Kline, of Mandan, left .Monday for
home, after a three day's business and
pleasure trip here. The boys let him off
easy and mounted him on a bronco that
only ran away with him four times. He
seemed to onjoy the round-up, but his
prediction that" the tender-foot will be
soro to-morrow," was vividly fulfilled.

We have received a note from Dr. E. E.
Ball, of Mandan, stating that on account

to lteep his engagement here until the
last of the month. As Dr. Ball is an ex

on his dates, which will be published in
time. -v.
